advisory.summary: ENG-17: _collect_records skips a dangling symlink (is_dir() and is_file() both False, no else branch), so tree_digest returns the digest of a partial tree instead of 'unavailable', contrary to its own docstring (lines 243-244).
advisory.fix: Raise OSError for an entry that is neither a directory nor a regular file (or check entry.is_symlink() for a broken target) so a dangling link records 'unavailable'; if a test is added, add the failure path to seam 4 through the orchestrator first (ENG-4).

advisory.summary: ENG-5: test_unreadable_subdirectory_is_unavailable_not_silently_skipped carries skipIf(os.geteuid() == 0) with no plan-stated exemption, so the declared seam 4 failure path is not exercised on root runs (CI runs ubuntu-latest as a non-root user, so it does run there).
advisory.fix: Make the path deterministic regardless of euid (e.g. patch os.scandir to raise PermissionError for the locked directory) and drop the skip, or declare the exemption and its reason in plan.md.

advisory.summary: ENG-24: the walker detects cycles only along the ancestor chain and keeps no visited set or work bound, so an acyclic symlink fan-out is re-walked once per path (measured 18.56 s at depth 14) and each file is still read whole; tree_digest runs before launch with no timeout. Operator-controlled trees only.
advisory.fix: Keep a visited set of realpaths across the whole walk (or treat a symlinked directory already hashed as 'unavailable'), cap total entries with 'unavailable' on overflow, and hash files in chunks.

advisory.summary: ENG-18: the combined no-bypass test reuses one --out for both harnesses, so the opencode run fails on out.mkdir(exist_ok=False) (bench.py:370) and the loop asserts nothing for opencode; return codes are unchecked.
advisory.fix: Use a per-harness output directory, assert returncode == 0 in each subTest, and assert two recorded calls.

advisory.summary: ENG-6: the New: reason for git_bytes/checkout_provenance rests on a tools/-only search; factory_cli.improvements.factory_sha already performs the rev-parse HEAD lookup and factory_cli.commands.git is an existing git subprocess helper.
advisory.fix: Reuse factory_sha for the revision (None -> 'unavailable') or extend the factory_cli git helper with a bytes/timeout option; correct the New: reasoning in a follow-up commit.

advisory.summary: ENG-25: the Claude Code grant (bare Read/Edit/Write, Bash(git:*), Bash(python3:*)) is not path-bounded and the launch inherits os.environ and the operator's HOME, so the 'confinement to the throwaway fixture is the control' line in claude-code.md:38 names a control the code does not enforce; the scoped no-bypass grant itself is the accepted brief Q2 decision.
advisory.fix: Set HOME for the launched process to the output directory (as isolated_install does) and/or narrow the Bash entries, or reword the residual-risk line to state that the grant reaches the operator account and a disposable environment is the control.

advisory.summary: ENG-26: in --from-checkout mode the isolated config's repo-layer skills are symlinks back into the live source checkout, so they sit outside every provenance digest and are writable through the Edit/Write grant.
advisory.fix: Copy repo-layer skills into <out>/harness-config/skills in checkout mode (or digest the full harness-config skills tree) and test that no link in the isolated config resolves outside <out>.

advisory.summary: ENG-25: out, home, harness-config and harness.log are created with the default umask while the golden-run procedure tells the operator to put a login or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in that config directory, and the run tree is retained.
advisory.fix: Create the run directories with mode 0o700 and harness.log with 0o600, and document credential file mode and run-tree retention.

advisory.summary: ENG-24: the harness launch and the checkout isolated-install subprocess.run calls have no timeout, so a hung agent or installer blocks the driver indefinitely.
advisory.fix: Pass generous timeouts, kill on expiry and report the timeout as the exit status.

advisory.summary: FR-007 and US4 AS5 require the installed factory revision, but installed_factory records only skill_dir and digest; research R5 and data-model.md chose the digest, so spec and plan disagree.
advisory.fix: Reconcile through the spec owner: record a revision (e.g. factory_sha or 'unavailable') beside the digest, or amend FR-007 to 'installed factory digest'.

advisory.summary: The OpenCode checklist defers headless smoke, pause/kill/resume, installed baseline and the PR leg to claude-code.md and never names tenluap/factory-golden-run-<date>, so it does not stand alone as FR-012, FR-014 and SC-006 require.
advisory.fix: Write the resume, installed-baseline and PR-leg steps (private tenluap/factory-golden-run-<date>, created at trial time, kept as evidence) into opencode.md itself.

advisory.summary: Both checklists route the cross-harness fallback to codex.md, which still holds unfilled placeholders, and claude-code.md:22 / opencode.md:22 cite the internal task id 'see T008' (SC-006, FR-012).
advisory.fix: Fill codex.md's placeholders from adapters/codex/harness.md or state in both checklists that the Codex fallback is not yet runnable; delete ', see T008' from both checklists.

advisory.summary: ENG-17: non-UTF-8 git output (checkout_provenance .decode()) or harness --version output (text=True) raises UnicodeDecodeError past the 'unavailable' handling and aborts the run before launch, contrary to FR-008.
advisory.fix: Decode with errors='replace' or catch UnicodeDecodeError into the 'unavailable' fallback.

advisory.summary: ENG-7: the user-facing benchmark guide still lists only --home/--out and says the driver always uses the installed factory; it omits --model, --from-checkout and <out>/provenance.json.
advisory.fix: Document --model, --from-checkout and the provenance.json output, qualifying the installed-factory sentence with 'unless --from-checkout is given'.
